name: Tabletop
source: A product told as a small physical set on a table: clay or felt or paper figures and props, a macro lens, a soft key light and a shallow depth of field, everything moving on twos like stop-motion. Described from the atlas clay-toy, diorama and paper-craft entries; no assets are carried.

frame_device.what: A tabletop set seen through a macro camera: a seamless paper or cloth sweep, a few handmade props and one hero figure; the table edge and a soft window light stay constant.
frame_device.moves: Figures hop, squash and settle on twos; the camera dollies a few centimetres per beat and racks focus between props; a hand-made prop slides in from off-table for each new idea.

ground_motion: The key light drifts a few degrees, dust motes and fabric fibres sit still but the boil wobble (a tiny seeded rotation per held frame) keeps every prop alive on twos.

type.classes: Chunky rounded or hand-cut type made as a physical object (clay letters, felt cut-outs, paper stencil) with one clean support face for the claim.
type.behaviour: Words are objects: they are placed, tipped and pulled out of frame by the same hands; the claim line is typeset sharp and fades in under the macro blur.

image.treatment: Soft physical materials (clay, gummy, felt, paper) with a believable key and fill, shallow depth of field, a faint table grain; Codex plates for backdrops and props, product UI as a small tablet or card prop.
image.behaviour: Everything moves on twos (12 fps) with squash and stretch; no smooth sliding, no motion blur; boil on outlines.

transitions: a hand-made prop wipes the frame (cloth pull, paper slide)
rack focus from one prop to the next
camera dolly through a gap between objects
the table turns on a lazy susan to the next set
squash-pop replace: one toy hops out as the next hops in

techniques.name: Hop on twos
techniques.what: A toy hops with a crouch, a stretch in the air, a landing squash and a settle, on held frames.
techniques.route: recipes/clay-toy.js build(k, {count, hopS, squash, stepFps: 12}); pose(t) is the held read of t; hits are the landings.

techniques.name: Macro rack focus
techniques.what: Focus slides from one tiny prop to the next while the camera creeps in.
techniques.route: Rasan3D camera keys with fstop 2 to 4 and focus distance keys per beat; recipe focus-pull.js between the props.

techniques.name: Diorama rise
techniques.what: A little block world rises on the table as the product's world.
techniques.route: recipes/voxel-diorama.js with a small grid (12 to 16); camera orbit 30 to 50 degrees.

techniques.name: Prop slide-in
techniques.what: A hand-made prop (a card, a sign, a screen) slides in from off-table to carry the next line.
techniques.route: Plane with a product plate or text texture; position key from off-frame, 0.4 s power3.out, 2 frame overshoot, held on twos.

techniques.name: Boil wobble
techniques.what: Outlines and props tremble by a hair each frame, the stop-motion tell.
techniques.route: clay-toy pose uses boil 0.2 to 0.5; or RasanShape.stepped(tl, {fps: 12}) and a seeded rotation per step on DOM props.

techniques.name: Cloth wipe
techniques.what: A cloth or paper sheet is pulled across the table and the next set is under it.
techniques.route: Full-frame textured plane or DOM layer translating x -120% to 120% on twos; the incoming scene sits beneath.

techniques.name: An object says the word
techniques.what: One toy or prop takes the stage as the beat's noun and the word sits beside it.
techniques.route: Hero toy to centre (x 0.4 s), word placed as a clay-lettered plane or sharp DOM text; others exit by hopping out.

techniques.name: Lazy-susan turn
techniques.what: The whole set turns to reveal the next scene on its back.
techniques.route: Parent group rotation.y 0 to 180 degrees over 1.0 s power2.inOut, held on twos; each side is a set.

techniques.name: Word choreography
techniques.what: Each word of a line enters from its own place and settles into the line with a lift; the key word last with a little more overshoot.
techniques.route: RasanShape.split on the sharp support face; words rise 20 px with a 4% squash on arrival, 0.5 s, stagger 0.08 s, key word last with back.out(1.4); object lettering is placed one letter per held frame.

signature: The last toy settles on its mark, the camera racks to the product card, and the table holds still for one beat with the claim in sharp type.

density.note: A hop, a rack or a prop change every 1.1 to 1.8 s; layers at the peak: 4 to 7 (sweep, set, hero toy, prop, light, support type).

palette.note: A brand palette dresses the toys and props; the soft light and the materials stay.

do: Keep every figure on twos with squash and stretch
Use one material family per film
Light it like a real tabletop: one key, one fill, soft shadow
Make each idea a physical prop that arrives by hand
Keep the claim in sharp type
dont: Do not slide or glide objects smoothly
Do not mix flat vector icons with clay props
Do not add glow, bloom or lens flare
Do not crowd the table; 3 props in a shot
